_comment: Vectors for FirstAmbiguousMember (Go) and firstAmbiguousMember (TypeScript). ambiguous: `want` is the path of the first member whose name folds onto an earlier one in the same object (Unicode simple folding, exact duplicates included), or null. invalid: each `document` is not exactly one valid JSON value, or nests deeper than the 10000 levels Go's encoding/json reads, and must be refused; where `detailContains` is given the refusal must carry it, so a depth vector is refused for its depth and not for some other fault. Entries in every section are named, and the runners report the name, never the document. The deepest documents read and the shallowest refused are spelled out in full, so each language's own depth limit is held to the same boundary. No two documents, and no two names, are identical. scoped: the same scan limited to a reader of the root object, FirstAmbiguousMemberIn (Go) and firstAmbiguousMemberIn (TypeScript): every root member name is checked, but only the values of the root members named in `read` are inspected, matched under the same folding; `want` is as in ambiguous. scopedInvalid: each `document` must be refused with `read` as given, since the members it does not inspect are still parsed.
